instruction: Create a single-page SVG showcase of a traditional Japanese kimono. Center the full garment silhouette and visibly include the T-shaped sleeves, crossed collar, wide obi sash, layered fabric, and an authentic nature-inspired repeating pattern. Use graceful folds, subtle depth, balanced negative space, and a restrained Japanese color palette. Put strong emphasis on elegant proportions, cultural specificity, visual coherence, and refined vector craft.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The full silhouette is not delivered — the garment is cropped at the bottom of the viewport (hem and lower body missing), so 'center the full garment' fails, and it sits in a left panel rather than acting as the page's central focal object. The crossed collar reads as a detached pale triangle floating above the V-neck with a center crease, not a left-over-right crossing band; 'layered fabric' is nearly absent (no visible front overlap edge, no under-collar/han-eri). The obi is narrower than 'wide,' and its central rounded shape reads as a front patch/button rather than a knot. The 'authentic nature-inspired repeating pattern' is a sparse rust speckle grid that reads as fabric noise, not a specific motif. Clarity & Hierarchy: The right column (heading, spec row, legend) is well organized, but annotation markers reinforce misreads — 01 points to the floating triangle, 04 to the obi's center patch — and the legend is cut off at the fold (03 half-visible). Low contrast between the beige garment and cream panel softens the silhouette edge, weakening the focal object; '1.24 × height' is cryptic. Visual System & Craft: Proportions are wrong — the body tapers narrower below the obi, but a kimono is a straight tube from shoulder to hem; sleeves are boxy rectangles with hard corners rather than graceful T-shapes; folds are a few faint lines with no depth shading; the garment is flat with no shadow, sitting on the panel like a sticker; the speckle grid is inconsistent in density and not seam-aligned; the gold under-obi band is a thin sliver. Expressiveness: The editorial frame (kanji seal, vertical 和装の美, Nº 01, gold hairlines, 'worn, not seen' headline) is genuinely distinctive, but the garment itself is generic — no chrysanthemum/maple/wave/asanoha motif, no visible hem or knot — so the memorable moments are missing. Real trade-off: strengthening the motif and adding depth risks breaking the restrained flat aesthetic; the resolution is one low-contrast motif plus subtle gradients, not busy ornament. A second trade-off: the two-column editorial layout gives context but pushes the garment off-center and causes the crop; the resolution is to keep the editorial frame but make the complete garment the dominant, fully-visible center.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all offline, self-contained SVG/CSS): 1) Silhouette first — redraw the kimono as a true T: constant-width, floor-length body with a gently curved hem, sized so the entire garment fits within the viewport with balanced negative space; widen the cream panel (or narrow the right text rail) so the complete garment is the centered focal object, nothing clipped. 2) Collar & layering — replace the floating triangle with a proper crossed collar band (left over right) running neck-to-chest, add a thin cream under-collar (han-eri) at the neckline, and draw the front overlap edge running down the body so 'layered fabric' is legible. 3) Obi — widen the sash to ~18–20% of body height, add a light obi-age band and a thin obi-jime, and read the knot as a back/taiko knot (or subtle front tie) rather than a center patch; keep the deep red with a soft vertical gradient. 4) Pattern — replace the speckle with one specific nature motif (e.g., small five-petal chrysanthemum or stylized maple) in rust/gold at ~15–20% contrast, tiled on a consistent grid across body and sleeves with seam-aligned continuity; keep collar and under-layer plain to show layering. 5) Folds & depth — add 4–6 graceful fold lines using paired light/dark strokes or subtle gradients at sleeve hems, under the obi, and at side seams; add a soft drop shadow beneath the garment and deepen the panel cream slightly (or add a hairline inner shadow) so the silhouette lifts off the ground. 6) Annotations & legend — reposition 01 to the actual crossed collar band and 04 to the obi-jime; thin the leader lines and shrink the red markers; ensure the full 01–05 legend is visible above the fold (or move it to a compact strip); clarify the length spec (e.g., '1.24 m — floor length'). 7) Polish pass — verify motif alignment across seams, soften sleeve-hem corners, curve the hem, and confirm no clipping at common viewport heights; retain the existing palette, typography, and editorial framing, which already carry the piece's identity.
